summary: GitHub Actions supply-chain tool pack. gha-audit.py statically audits workflow YAML against 14 rules, each drawn from a real 2025-26 incident — a mutable action tag (tj-actions/changed-files, CVE-2025-30066, ~23k repos retagged), a pull-request title interpolated into run: (Nx s1ngularity, 2,180 accounts), pull_request_target checking out the fork's head, toJSON(secrets) or a secret beside curl (GhostAction, 3,325 secrets), missing permissions, permissions write-all, workflow-scope id-token, missing concurrency or timeout-minutes, ubuntu-22.04, persist-credentials left at its default, curl piped to sh — and prints only the offending line, its severity and the fix, failing at or above --fail-on. gha-pin.py resolves every uses: owner/repo@tag to the 40-char commit SHA through the GitHub API, rewrites it in place with the tag kept as a comment, and --check is the drift gate that keeps a repository pinned. Workflows are read by an indentation-aware mini-lexer, not a YAML parser, because a tool pack ships no dependencies.

credentials.min_scope: no scope at all for public repositories — a classic PAT with no boxes ticked, or a fine-grained token with Public repositories, read-only; the token buys the 5,000/hour rate limit, not access. gha-audit reads no credential and opens no socket.
